neighbours.label: ' to' starting an infinitive after a readiness or tendency predicate (poised to, set to, tends to)
fire: The startup is poised to become the largest seller in the region.
Analysts say the bank is poised to raise interest rates next month.
Coastal storms tend to weaken quickly once they reach land.
The new stadium is set to open in the spring of next year.
Young children tend to copy what their parents do.
The senator appears poised to announce her candidacy on Friday.
Electric cars are poised to overtake petrol cars in sales.
Older laptops tend to overheat when running heavy software.
quiet: The startup moved to a larger office in the center of the region.
Analysts sent the report to the bank before the meeting next month.
Coastal storms brought heavy rain to the villages along the shore.
The new stadium belongs to the city and opens in the spring.
Young children listen to stories before they go to sleep.
The senator spoke to reporters outside the building on Friday.
Electric cars are sold to buyers in many countries now.
Older laptops were given to the school after the upgrade.

notes: Card flags broad (2.8%), max 0.28; top 32 are mostly ' to' after poised/tends. Probe: 'poised to' 0.56, 'tend to' 0.14, plain 'to' ~0.05.
